courses.summary: Are you passionate about understanding what connects and disrupts communities, the nation, and the world? Do you appreciate the power of narratives in the past and present that shape the future? Forge global citizenship and a meaningful career path by choosing from a range of major and minor study areas in the arts, humanities and languages. This degree program develops your love of reading, evaluating and writing into career-based skills for critiquing, curating, exhibiting, communicating and shaping knowledge about the place of people in the world. Explore ideas, theories and records of human interaction and more-than-human relationships with nature and artificial intelligence. Gain advanced skills in history, literature, language, politics, society and culture.
courses.careers: Employment options for graduates are linked with your chosen areas of specialisation and may include roles in local, state and commonwealth public service, non-government organisations, higher education, museums, libraries and archives, arts and cultural organisations, as well as other diverse sectors which are increasingly calling for employees possessing skills developed by the Bachelor of Arts.
courses.practicalExperience: Students will complete a minimum 140-hour placement in the second or third year of their degree program. There will be a variety of opportunities available to undertake a placement in their desired career field, including museums, libraries and archives, arts and cultural organisations, non-government organisations, and local, state and commonwealth public service.

courses.summary: Construction management graduates work in a range of leadership roles in the industry. This includes project management, contract management, quantity surveying, estimating, building surveying, building certification, facilities management, property development and WHS. They manage physical buildings and infrastructure projects, working onsite, in an office, or a combination of both. Construction managers lead and coordinate design and construction processes. They liaise with clients and consultants, and select, hire and supervise various contractors. They’re also responsible for managing the legal and financial aspects of the project.

courses.practicalExperience: Career-ready placements allow you to integrate real-world skills and experience with theoretical concepts and knowledge obtained during your studies. courses.summary: Surveyors help plan, measure, and manage the world around us. From infrastructure and land development to environmental monitoring and digital construction, surveying plays a critical role in how communities grow, connect, and respond to change. The Bachelor of Surveying (Honours) combines surveying expertise with emerging technologies in spatial data science, satellite positioning, remote sensing and digital mapping. You’ll learn how advanced technologies are used to capture, analyse and manage spatial information to support infrastructure, land development, and environmental decision-making. The University of Newcastle's Surveying programs have been designed to prepare graduates for the future of the profession through a combination of flexible study, practical field experience and industry engagement. Study flexibly through a combination of online learning and dedicated on-campus field intensives, allowing you to develop practical surveying skills while accessing a high-quality university education from a wider range of locations.
courses.careers: Surveyors are sought after across infrastructure, construction, land development, mining, environmental management and spatial technologies by government agencies, consulting firms and major infrastructure projects. As a result, graduates enjoy diverse career pathways and the opportunity to contribute to projects that shape communities and support economic growth. Career opportunities may include; Geospatial Specialist, Hydrographic Surveyor, Mining Surveyor, Photogrammetrist, Registered Land Surveyor and Town Planning. Surveying is a profession experiencing strong demand across New South Wales and Australia, creating excellent employment opportunities for graduates.
courses.practicalExperience: Students develop practical surveying skills through supervised on-campus field intensives, where they gain hands-on experience using contemporary surveying equipment and industry-standard workflows. In addition, all University of Newcastle engineering students complete 12 weeks of industrial experience during their degree. This can be undertaken as a single placement or as shorter placements of no less than two weeks, providing valuable professional experience, industry networks and opportunities to apply classroom learning in real-world settings.

courses.name: Diploma in Surveying
courses.area: Surveying principles, surveying measurements, land and engineering surveying, satellite positioning (GNSS), geospatial technologies, digital mapping, geographic information systems (GIS), spatial data collection and analysis, mathematics, land management, and practical fieldwork through on-campus field intensives.
courses.assumed: Mathematics Advanced (Band 5). Applicants who have achieved less than Band 5 may need additional study and/or assistance to successfully complete the mathematics requirement of the program.
courses.fees: Refer to University of Newcastle current fee information .
courses.summary: Surveyors play an important role in shaping infrastructure, land development and communities. From construction and mining projects to spatial mapping and environmental management, surveying professionals help collect and manage the data used to plan and develop the world around us. The Diploma in Surveying provides a practical introduction to surveying principles, fieldwork practices and modern surveying methods. Designed to be completed in one year, this program develops foundational skills in surveying methods, measurements, spatial data and land management, preparing you for entry-level roles in the surveying industry. The program combines online learning with compulsory on-campus field intensives, supporting flexible study while maintaining essential practical surveying experience. Graduates may continue their studies in the Bachelor of Surveying (Honours), with credit towards the degree, or move directly into the workforce.
courses.careers: Surveyors are involved in the planning of almost all development and mapping of the land and earth. A shortage of surveyors in Australia has led to high demand for graduates. This program will prepare you with the basic knowledge and practical skills for entry-level surveying positions. These positions may include an assistant land surveyor, geospatial analyst, or survey technician.
courses.practicalExperience: The program includes supervised on-campus field intensives that provide practical experience with contemporary surveying equipment and field techniques, allowing students to apply theoretical knowledge in real-world surveying exercises.

courses.name: Open Foundation
courses.area: Open Foundation courses cover a range of disciplines, including business and entrepreneurship; computing, maths and technology; communications and creative industries; education; health and medical services; law; science and the environment and society and culture. It is important to consider the undergraduate degree you’d like to study upon completion of Open Foundation, as the courses you choose help to prepare you for that area of study. If you are not sure what degree you would like to study, you can speak to a Student Liaison Officer, Careers Advisor, and other free resources to help you choose your degree destination.
courses.prerequisites: Open Foundation serves as a pathway to university studies. While applicants are not required to have completed prior studies, they must be 17 years or older at the time of submitting an application.
courses.additionalCriteria: Open Foundation serves as a pathway to university studies. While applicants are not required to have completed prior studies, they must be 17 years or older at the time of submitting an application.
courses.fees: Refer to University of Newcastle current fee information .
courses.summary: Open Foundation is a free pathway program offered at the University of Newcastle for people who do not have the qualifications required for direct entry into their desired undergraduate degree program or for those who feel they could use a little extra preparation and support before beginning their degree. It is designed to help you develop the skills you need not only to gain entry, but to find success at university and beyond. Upon completion, Open Foundation offers guaranteed entry into over 70 undergraduate degrees at the University of Newcastle. If you are not sure what you’d like to study, Open Foundation offers you the opportunity to explore your options with a wide range of courses across several popular disciplines. You can also choose to study either 4 or 6 courses, to help you decide what undergraduate program suits you. You will receive embedded support from the Pathways team, including access to a dedicated Student Liaison Officer, a quiet space to complete your independent study, Peer Assisted Study Sessions (PASS) and personal and careers counselling should you require it. Open Foundation also offers flexibility. By passing 40 units of courses, you can complete the program in just one semester, or study for up to two years part time, depending on the number of courses and flexibility options you choose. Study at our Newcastle (Callaghan) or Central Coast (Gosford) campus, online, or a combination to suit. Upon completion, you will receive a Certificate of Attainment and a Selection Rank equivalent, which is recognised as an entry qualification for many universities across Australia. We recommend you place Open Foundation as your fifth preference or higher, to ensure you begin your studies in the next intake.
courses.careers: Upon successful completion of the program, students are guaranteed entry into a selection of undergraduate degrees at the University of Newcastle and are eligible to apply for admission to most degree programs. Completion of Open Foundation is accepted as an entry qualification to many universities in Australia. Open Foundation may be used to determine eligibility for 785000 Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine (Joint Medical Program) via the Excellence Through Equity Pathway to Medicine .
